title: Does Sugar Make Kids Hyper? What Studies Found
description:
A 1995 JAMA meta-analysis of 23 blinded studies found sugar did not affect children's behaviour or cognition (a small effect in some children can't be ruled out). In one study, mothers told their child had sugar rated them as more hyperactive even when it was a placebo. Sugar still matters for teeth and weight.

Sources:
• Wolraich ML et al. The effect of sugar on behavior or cognition in children: a meta-analysis. JAMA 1995: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7474248/
• Vreeman RC, Carroll AE. Festive medical myths. BMJ 2008: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19091758/
• Hoover DW, Milich R. Effects of sugar ingestion expectancies on mother-child interactions. 1994: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7963081/

✅ Fact-checked as of 23 Nov 2026. Medical evidence and guidelines change; check the sources above for updates.
